national_news.title: Union Cabinet Approves Continuation and Renaming of National Social Assistance Programme
bullets: The Union Cabinet approved the continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with a total outlay of Rs 53,428 crore.

The program has been renamed as Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana, along with the renaming of sub-schemes like Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme to Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana.

Eligibility criteria for divyangjan pension were revised, lowering the benchmark disability requirement to 40 percent and fixing the assistance rate at Rs 375 (up to 79 years) and Rs 625 (80 years and above) benefiting around 3.2 crore people across all States and UTs.

national_news.title: India Condemns Attacks on Civil Infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and Expresses Solidarity
bullets: India expressed strong solidarity with Saudi Arabia and condemned the recent string of attacks on civil infrastructure, including the Aramco headquarters.
External Affairs Ministry stated that such attacks on civil infrastructure are unacceptable and must cease immediately, affirming support for Saudi sovereignty.
MEA also criticized the UN Human Rights Commission (OHCHR) for its selective approach regarding law enforcement actions and protests, warning that it undermines multilateralism.

national_news.title: IEA Warns Fragile Oil Supply Recovery Amid Repeated Gulf Attacks
bullets: The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned in its monthly Oil Market Report that repeated attacks in the Gulf have made global oil supply recovery fragile.
Global oil supply is projected to decline to 100.7 million bpd this year before rebounding in 2027.
Global oil demand is forecast to fall by an average of 2.6 million barrels per day in 2026 due to West Asian conflicts and soaring fuel prices.

national_news.title: EAM S Jaishankar Emphasizes India's Role as a 'Power in the Middle' at Bloomberg New Economy Forum
bullets: External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar stated at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that the world is transitioning toward a new international order shaped by middle powers.
He clarified that India does not identify as a 'middle power' but as a 'power in the middle', citing its status as the world's most populous nation with a USD 4 trillion GDP.
He emphasized that the era of a single country dictating terms through threats is over, and nations are increasingly pursuing independent policies and mutual agreements.

national_news.title: India's Public Debt-to-GDP Ratio Declines to 55% Over Five Years, Says Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw
bullets: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced that India's public debt-to-GDP ratio has fallen from 61% to 55% over the past five years.
Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, he highlighted India's ambition to become a trusted partner in semiconductor design, manufacturing, and testing.
The minister noted that India is replicating its successful mobile manufacturing ecosystem approach—moving from assembly to component exports—into the semiconductor, railway, and defense sectors.

national_news.title: EAM S. Jaishankar Outlines Evolution of New International Order
bullets: External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar spoke at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, stating the era of a single country dictating terms through threats is over.
Dr. Jaishankar clarified that India identifies as a 'power in the middle' rather than a 'middle power', citing its status as the world's most populous nation with a $4 trillion GDP.
He emphasized that consensus, mutual understanding, and self-interest will drive the enforcement of rules among middle powers in the emerging international order.

national_news.title: President Droupadi Murmu Emphasizes Scientific Cooperation for National Security
bullets: President Droupadi Murmu stated that modern national security extends beyond traditional military capabilities, requiring close cooperation between scientific institutions and the armed forces.
She addressed the faculty and course members of the 66th National Defence College Course at Rashtrapati Bhavan, highlighting the expansion of warfare into cyber security, space, and biotechnology.
The President underlined the significance of government initiatives like the Research, Development and Innovation Scheme in bridging innovation and national security.

national_news.title: India Hosts First BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi
bullets: Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi, emphasizing regional integration and collective security.
He reaffirmed India's policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism and called for real-time intelligence sharing, mutual legal assistance, and extradition cooperation.
BIMSTEC, established in 1997, comprises seven member states: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand.

national_news.title: Shafali Verma and Shubman Gill Named ICC Players of the Month for September 2026
bullets: Indian opener Shafali Verma won the ICC Women’s Player of the Month for September 2026 following stellar performances in the Women’s Asia Cup and Asian Games.
Indian captain Shubman Gill secured the ICC Men’s Player of the Month award for a record fifth time after scoring 333 runs in the ODI series against the West Indies.
Gill's stellar outings included a century and an unbeaten double century, extending his record for the most monthly awards in men's cricket.

national_news.title: Indian Coast Guard Inducts Indigenous ALH MK-III Helicopter in Maharashtra
bullets: The Indian Coast Guard inducted its first indigenous Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH MK-III) aircraft, CG 875, into the Coast Guard Region (West) at Ratnagiri, Maharashtra.
The helicopter is equipped with an Advanced Radar, Electro Optical Pod, Automatic Identification System, and a cabin-mounted 12.7 mm Heavy Machine Gun.

This induction is the first of five allotted ALH MK-III aircraft to be positioned with 831 Sqn (CG) at Ratnagiri to enhance maritime surveillance and security within the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

national_news.title: New Delhi Launches EV Charging Stations and Air Quality Monitoring Stations
bullets: Union Minister for Environment and Forests Bhupender Yadav and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta launched five public EV charging stations and 13 new Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations in New Delhi.
The initiative aims to strengthen real-time monitoring of the Air Quality Index (AQI) across the national capital.
The Delhi government expanded its combined fleet of electric and CNG buses to over 5,500 units in line with commitments made to the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM).

national_news.title: Ministry of Railways Announces Pan-India Rail Jan Samvaad for October 2026
bullets: The Ministry of Railways scheduled a citizen-centric pan-India 'Rail Jan Samvaad' across all railway stations on October 22, 2026, as part of Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6 (SCDPM-6).
Indian Railways set nationwide targets to clean 1,00,000 sites, free 7,00,000 sq. ft. of space, and generate ₹600 crore through scrap and e-waste disposal by the end of the month.
The campaign emphasizes effective collection, segregation, and disposal of e-waste as per the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

national_news.title: Indian Navy Commissions INS Mangrol, Mahe-Class ASW SWC
bullets: INS Mangrol (P82), the third Mahe-class Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC), was commissioned into the Indian Navy at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai on October 12, 2026.
The ship is indigenously designed and constructed by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi, featuring over 80 percent indigenous content to support Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
It is equipped for Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), underwater surveillance, Low-Intensity Maritime Operations (LIMO), and mine warfare tasks in coastal and shallow waters.

national_news.title: KVIC Performance and Growth of Khadi & Village Industries
bullets: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) is a statutory body established under the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956.
In FY 2025-26, sales of Khadi and Village Industries products reached a historic ₹1.87 lakh crore, showing a 501% growth compared to 2013-14.
Employment in the sector increased by 56% to 2.04 crore, with women constituting over 80% of artisans in the Khadi sector and over 59% of total trainees under KVIC programs.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Uses AI to Restore Ancient Mundeshwari Temple
bullets: The Mundeshwari Temple in Kaimur district, Bihar, is dedicated to Maa Durga and Lord Shiva and is believed to be the world's oldest functional Hindu temple, dating back to 108 CE.
The site has been protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) since 1915.

The Bihar Heritage Development Society (BHDS) has initiated a scientific process using 3D measurements and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to reconstruct the original Nagara-style form of the temple from scattered architectural debris.

bihar_news.title: ICAR-MGIFRI Organizes Training on Crop Management in Flood-Affected Lands
bullets: ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute (ICAR-MGIFRI), Motihari, organized a three-day residential training programme on post-flood crop management in Diara and Chaur lands.
The programme was sponsored by the Bihar Agricultural Management and Extension Training Institute (BAMETI), Patna.
Key focus areas included climate-resilient farming, zero-tillage, residual soil moisture utilization, and Integrated Farming Systems (IFS) combining crop, livestock, and aquatic resources.

bihar_news.title: Gaya Named Best Performer Under PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
bullets: Gaya (Bihar), Nagaur (Rajasthan), and Umaria (Madhya Pradesh) were recognized as the best-performing aspirational districts in the first year of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY).
PM-DDKY integrates 36 central schemes across 11 ministries with an annual outlay of ₹24,000 crore, targeting low crop productivity, low cropping intensity, and low agricultural credit disbursement.
Union Agriculture Minister announced the 'Khet Bachao Abhiyan' to be held from October 22 to November 30, 2026, to promote soil health and balanced fertilizer use.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Aims to Become Hub of Entrepreneurship and Innovation
bullets: Bihar aims to become a major hub of entrepreneurship, employment, and innovation under the double-engine government.
The state cabinet resolved to make Bihar an active participant in building a developed India by 2047.
Over Rs 13 lakh crore has been directly transferred to the Bihar government by the Centre over the last 12 years.

bihar_news.title: Bodh Gaya Emporium Plan to Expand Market Access for Bihar's Jeevika Women
bullets: The Bihar Rural Development Department directed the expedited construction of an emporium at Bodh Gaya to provide Jeevika women access to domestic and international buyers.
Similar facilities are planned at other major tourist destinations in the state to showcase local handicrafts and traditional artworks.
Additional initiatives include establishing block-level Sudha milk outlets operated by Jeevika women and organizing the Saras fair at Gandhi Maidan from December 12 to 28.
